newsitem.title: GERMANY: Top German ad executive says TV ad limits harmful.
newsitem.headline: Top German ad executive says TV ad limits harmful.

text.p: One of Germany's top advertising executives called on Monday for the lifting of the country's ban on advertising during television news broadcasts, saying it led to worse and not better news programming.
Willi Schalk, chief executive of advertising giant McCann-Erickson's German group, told Reuters that especially private broadcasters' news programming suffered from a lack of advertising funding.

"A good editorial news division costs a station at least 100 million marks ($60 million) a year, with no ad income to offset that," Schalk said. "If television does not want to lose it market share for ads, a loosening of this type of ban is essential."
Schalk also described as absurd the restriction of advertising on German public broadcasting after 8 p.m.
"With this exclusion, you allow advertising on public television, but you hardly give it the chance to reach its target groups," he said.
Schalk said television's loss in Germany may add up to gains for direct marketing and interactive media.
"Each form of advertising than reaches the targeted consumer wins on attractiveness," Schalk said. ($ = 1.668 German Marks)
